recentItems.title: Sky over Moscow CLOSED! Hundreds of flights canceled over fear of Ukrainian drones
recentItems.description:
Ukraine is stepping up long-range strikes on Russia's strategic assets: the port of Sochi came under attack, while one of Russia's largest oil refineries halted processing operations. Moscow airports faced flight cancellations and delays for a second consecutive night. Meanwhile, the EU is preparing billions of euros to bolster Ukrainian air defense, and Germany will deliver IRIS-T missiles along with thousands of drones. Another key focus is the incident at Leipzig Airport, which German authorities attribute to Russia. Berlin and the EU are preparing new restrictions and escalating pressure on Moscow.

recentItems.title: Minus $1.1B in 7 days: How Ukraine BURNS Russian economy and air defense
recentItems.description:
Ukraine continues to launch high-precision strikes against Russia's key strategic and military assets. Over the past week, major oil refineries, the Ust-Luga oil terminal, military airfields, radars, and air defense systems all came under attack. Reports highlight damage to a Tu-95MS strategic bomber and a high-value "Nebo-U" radar system. According to the calculations presented in this report, Russian equipment losses alone reached an estimated $1.1 billion in just seven days. At the same time, strikes on energy infrastructure compound the strain on Kremlin revenues and its capacity to fund the war.

recentItems.title: Ukraine SHATTERS Kremlin's plans in Donbas | Sky over Moscow BLOCKED — airports closed
recentItems.description:
Ukraine’s Defense Forces have inflicted new losses on the Russian military. The General Staff confirmed the destruction of a Russian MiG-29 fighter jet and a Ka-27 helicopter. In addition, Ukrainian forces struck critical Russian rear logistics facilities in Donetsk region — an ammunition depot in Volodymyrivka and a supply depot in Ocheretyne. At the same time, the situation on the front line remains tense, with the fiercest fighting ongoing in the Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk directions. Watch the video for full details on Russian aviation losses, strikes on enemy logistics, and the latest frontline updates.

recentItems.title: "Naked Emperor" in Bishkek: SCO Summit turns into total failure for Kremlin
recentItems.description:
The SCO summit failed to deliver the support the Kremlin had hoped for: the final declaration once again omitted any mention of Russia’s war against Ukraine, while Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a shift from hostilities to peace. Meanwhile, Putin rejected ceasefire demands, threatened new strikes on Ukraine’s energy grid, and denied preparations for another mobilization. Against the backdrop of oil refining crises, sanctions, and the lack of significant battlefield successes, a key question emerges: why does the Kremlin keep raising the stakes, and is ending the war becoming a direct threat to Putin’s own power?

recentItems.title: One shot — 14 POWs: "Group 200" Rubizh Brigade warrior's story
recentItems.description:
In this video, a warrior call-signed "Raptor" gives a raw account of the "Group 200" assault unit within the "Rubizh" Brigade. You’ll hear real frontline stories: from how their name originated as dark humor during the battles for Rubizhne, to complex night assaults orchestrated by commanders like a game of chess. Raptor remembers the brave commander Roys, shares the pain of losing brothers-in-arms Kutsyi and Kirpich under heavy enemy artillery fire, and details a successful operation that captured 14 Russian prisoners. This is a tough, honest story of military brotherhood, combat losses, life-saving dark humor on the front lines, and the unyielding resilience of Ukrainian defenders who keep fighting.
